description: Forward from Gmail automatically: instead of setting up a Gmail forwarding filter (which needs Gmail's settings on a computer, or Chrome in desktop mode on Android), TrackerHacker picks up mail from the person's hacks' senders in their Gmail itself, like a forwarding filter, within seconds of it arriving, plus up to 25 such emails from the last 30 days when turned on, and again for a sender a hack gains while it's on. Save the hack before giving the link, so the person sees their sheet fill. It opens only those messages and stores no email; senderList says exactly whose mail it picks up, and a sender that is a whole personal mail domain (gmail.com, outlook.com) never is (notPickedUp), though a full address at one (someone@gmail.com) is picked up like any other; it is not a way to read their email in general (for that, use your own Gmail connection). It's one tap on Google's Allow screen, on any device. Returns whether it's offered and on, and the link the person opens to turn it on. Only they can tap Allow; you can't turn it on for them. Google's screen says TrackerHacker could read all their email, because Google has no narrower permission; TrackerHacker only opens mail from their hacks' senders. Until Google finishes reviewing it, Google first shows a "Google hasn't verified this app" warning they tap through (Advanced, then Go to TrackerHacker). Hacks with no senders list aren't forwarded this way. To turn it off, stop_gmail_reading.
name: read_gmail
title: Forward from Gmail automatically
